# Screenshot Plan — Technical Debt Accountant

## Screenshots

### 1. Add Debt Dialog
**Title:** Log Technical Debt at Your Cursor with Alt+D
**What to capture:** The Add Debt dialog open over the editor, showing fields for category (dropdown with 9 options), priority, description, estimated fix time, and tags. The file path and line should be auto-filled.

### 2. Tech Debt Tool Window
**Title:** Debt Inventory at a Glance
**What to capture:** The Tech Debt tool window at the bottom of the IDE showing a table of debt items with columns for file, category, priority, status, workaround minutes, and cost. Include several items across different categories and priorities.

### 3. Gutter Icons
**Title:** Priority-Colored Gutter Icons with Debt Tooltips
**What to capture:** The editor showing colored gutter icons (red for Critical, orange for High, yellow for Medium, green for Low) next to lines with debt items. Show the tooltip popup for one of the icons.

### 4. Hotspot Detection
**Title:** Identify Your Most Expensive Files
**What to capture:** The hotspot view in the tool window showing the top files ranked by weighted debt score. Include file paths, item counts, and scores.

### 5. Dollar Valuation (Pro)
**Title:** See the Dollar Cost of Every Debt Item
**What to capture:** The tool window showing debt items with dollar amounts — workaround cost, estimated fix cost, and monthly interest columns visible. Show a total at the bottom.

### 6. ROI Calculator (Pro)
**Title:** Prioritize Refactoring by Return on Investment
**What to capture:** The ROI view showing debt items sorted by breakeven months, with columns for fix cost, monthly interest, and ROI ranking. Highlight the top opportunities.

### 7. Management Report (Pro)
**Title:** Executive-Ready Debt Report in One Click
**What to capture:** A generated Markdown report rendered in a preview, showing the executive summary, priority breakdown, top hotspots, and ROI opportunities sections.

### 8. Burndown Chart (Pro)
**Title:** Track Debt Resolution Trends Over Time
**What to capture:** The burndown chart showing debt count or cost over time with a trend indicator (IMPROVING, STABLE, or WORSENING).
